title: Wishes and requests: quiero que vengas
summary: Want, hope, ask, advise, allow or forbid someone else to do something with que + subjunctive; keep the infinitive when it's the same person.
focus: Infinitive vs. que + present subjunctive after verbs of wishing and influence; decir que; ojalá and set wishes
content:
## Same person or someone else?

With **querer**, **esperar**, **preferir** and **necesitar**, ask who does the second action. Same person: the **infinitive**. Someone else: **que + subjunctive**.

| verb | same person | someone else |
|---|---|---|
| querer | **Quiero ir.** (I want to go.) | **Quiero que vayas.** (I want you to go.) |
| esperar | **Espero llegar pronto.** | **Espero que llegues pronto.** |
| preferir | **Prefiero cocinar yo.** | **Prefiero que cocines tú.** |
| necesitar | **Necesito descansar.** | **Necesito que me ayudes.** |

English says *I want you to go*; Spanish says *I want that you go*: **quiero que vayas**. Never *quiero que ir*, and never *quiero que vaya* when you are the one going.

## Asking, advising, allowing, forbidding

Verbs that push someone else to act take **que + subjunctive**: **pedir** (to ask), **recomendar**, **aconsejar** (to advise), **permitir** (to allow) and **prohibir** (to forbid), usually with an indirect pronoun for the person.

- **Te pido que me esperes.** I'm asking you to wait for me.
- **Le recomiendo que pruebe el pescado.** I recommend you try the fish. (usted)
- **Os aconsejo que salgáis temprano.** I advise you to leave early.
- **Mi jefe no permite que comamos en la oficina.** My boss doesn't let us eat in the office.
- **Nos prohíben que aparquemos aquí.** They forbid us to park here.

**Permitir** and **prohibir** may also take a plain infinitive: **te prohíbo salir**. Watch the accent: **prohíbo, prohíbe**.

## Decir: telling or reporting

**Decir** has two jobs, and the mood shows which one:

| sentence | meaning | mood |
|---|---|---|
| **Dice que viene.** | She says she's coming. (a report) | indicative |
| **Me dice que venga.** | She tells me to come. (an order) | subjunctive |

- **Ana dice que tiene hambre.** Ana says she's hungry.
- **Ana nos dice que comamos ya.** Ana tells us to eat now.

After a past verb (*me dijo que viniera*) Spanish uses the imperfect subjunctive, which you meet at B2.

## Ojalá and good wishes

**Ojalá** (*I hope*, *let's hope*) always takes the subjunctive, with or without **que**: **Ojalá (que) llueva.** Let's hope it rains.

A bare **que** + subjunctive makes a ready-made wish (an unspoken *espero* in front):

- **¡Que te mejores!** Get well soon!
- **¡Que aproveche!** Enjoy your meal!
- **¡Que tengas suerte!** Good luck!
- **¡Que lo pases bien!** Have a good time!

The verb follows the person: **¡Que se mejore!** (usted), **¡Que lo paséis bien!** (vosotros).

vocabulary.example: Quiero que vengas a mi cumpleaños.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I want you to come to my birthday party.

vocabulary.example: Espero que te guste el regalo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope you like the present.

vocabulary.example: Prefiero que hablemos mañana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd rather we talked tomorrow.

vocabulary.example: Necesito que me prestes tu coche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I need you to lend me your car.

vocabulary.example: Le pido al camarero que nos traiga la cuenta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I ask the waiter to bring us the bill.

vocabulary.example: Os recomiendo que visitéis Toledo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I recommend that you visit Toledo.

vocabulary.example: Mi profesora me aconseja que lea en español.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My teacher advises me to read in Spanish.

vocabulary.example: El dueño prohíbe que fumemos en el piso.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The owner forbids us to smoke in the flat.

vocabulary.example: Mis padres no permiten que mi hermano use el móvil en la mesa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My parents don't let my brother use his phone at the table.

vocabulary.meaning: to say that (+ indicative) / to tell (someone) to (+ subjunctive)
vocabulary.example: Mi madre me dice que vuelva pronto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My mother tells me to come back early.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá aprobemos el examen.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope we pass the exam.

vocabulary.example: ¿Tienes gripe? ¡Que te mejores!
vocabulary.example_meaning: You've got the flu? Get well soon!

vocabulary.example: Veo que estáis comiendo. ¡Que aproveche!
vocabulary.example_meaning: I see you're eating. Enjoy your meal!

vocabulary.example: Mañana tienes la entrevista, ¿no? ¡Que tengas suerte!
vocabulary.example_meaning: Your interview is tomorrow, isn't it? Good luck!

quiz.prompt: Esta noche estoy cansada. Prefiero ___ en casa.
quiz.explanation: The same person prefers and stays, so the infinitive: prefiero quedarme. 'Que me quede' is only for someone else.
hints: Who prefers? Who stays? The same person?

quiz.prompt: Mis padres quieren que yo ___ medicina.
quiz.explanation: The parents want, I study: two different people, so que + subjunctive: estudie.
hints: Different subjects after querer take que + subjunctive.
-ar verbs swap to -e in the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Espero que ___ (tú, tener) un buen viaje.
quiz.explanation: Esperar que + a different subject takes the subjunctive. Tengo becomes tenga, then tengas.
hints: Start from the yo form: tengo.

quiz.prompt: El médico me recomienda que ___ (beber) más agua.
quiz.explanation: Recomendar que pushes someone else to act: subjunctive. Bebo becomes beba.
hints: -er verbs swap to -a in the subjunctive.
Who drinks? Me, the patient: yo.

quiz.prompt: Te pido que no ___ (llegar, tú) tarde mañana.
quiz.explanation: Pedir que + subjunctive. Llegar keeps its hard g sound with gu: llegue, llegues.
hints: Spelling: g becomes gu before e.

quiz.prompt: Ana dice que ___ muy cansada. (She is reporting how she feels.)
quiz.explanation: Decir que reports a fact here, so the indicative: Ana dice que está cansada.

quiz.prompt: Mi madre me dice que ___ mi habitación. (She tells me to tidy it.)
quiz.explanation: Decir que as an order (tell someone to) takes the subjunctive: ordene.
hints: An order with decir takes the subjunctive.

quiz.explanation: Ojalá always takes the subjunctive. Hago becomes haga.
hints: Start from the yo form: hago.

quiz.prompt: Your friend has a bad cold. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: ¡Que te mejores! wishes someone a quick recovery. ¡Que aproveche! is for a meal, ¡Que lo pases bien! for a party or trip, ¡Que tengas suerte! for an exam or interview.

conversations.title: A favour for the weekend
conversations.scenario: Clara is going away for the weekend and asks her flatmate Diego to look after the flat and the cat.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Diego, este fin de semana me voy a Sevilla. ¿Puedo pedirte un favor?
lines.meaning: Diego, I'm off to Seville this weekend. Can I ask you a favour?

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Of course. What do you need?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Necesito que riegues mis plantas el sábado.
lines.meaning: I need you to water my plants on Saturday.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí. Te pido que no abras la ventana del salón.
lines.meaning: Yes. Please don't open the living-room window.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tranquila. ¿Prefieres que te mande fotos del gato?
lines.meaning: Don't worry. Would you like me to send you photos of the cat?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Sí, por favor! Ojalá no se aburra sin mí.
lines.meaning: Yes, please! I hope he doesn't get bored without me.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Mi madre dice que los gatos no echan de menos a nadie.
lines.meaning: My mother says cats don't miss anybody.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué malo eres! Bueno, me voy ya.
lines.meaning: You're so mean! Right, I'm off.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Que tengas buen viaje y que lo pases muy bien!
lines.meaning: Have a good trip and have a great time!

listening.text: Quiero que me escuches.
listening.meaning: I want you to listen to me.

listening.text: Necesito que me ayudes hoy.
listening.meaning: I need you to help me today.

listening.text: Ojalá no llueva este fin de semana.
listening.meaning: I hope it doesn't rain this weekend.

listening.text: Mi jefa prefiere que trabajemos desde casa.
listening.meaning: My boss prefers us to work from home.
listening.note: New word: la jefa = the boss.

listening.text: Te recomiendo que pruebes el gazpacho de este bar.
listening.meaning: I recommend you try the gazpacho in this bar.
listening.note: New word: el gazpacho = cold tomato soup.

listening.text: Los vecinos nos piden que no hagamos ruido por la noche.
listening.meaning: The neighbours ask us not to make noise at night.
listening.note: New word: el ruido = the noise.

listening.text: Espero que lo paséis muy bien en la boda de vuestros amigos.
listening.meaning: I hope you have a great time at your friends' wedding.

listening.text: Mi hermano dice que está bien, pero yo quiero que vaya al médico.
listening.meaning: My brother says he's fine, but I want him to go to the doctor.
listening.note: Decir que reports with the indicative; querer que asks with the subjunctive.

guide.tip: One person doing both: quiero venir. Two people: quiero que vengas. With decir, ask: a report (indicative) or an order (subjunctive)?

bites.title: One person: infinitive
bites.rule: If the one who wants, hopes or prefers is also the one who acts, use the infinitive: quiero ir, espero aprobar, prefiero cocinar.
bites.example_meaning: I need to rest a little.

bites.title: Someone else: que + subjunctive
bites.rule: When you want, ask, advise, allow or forbid someone ELSE to act: querer / pedir / aconsejar / permitir / prohibir que + subjunctive.
bites.example_meaning: I advise you to leave early.

bites.title: Decir: report or order
bites.rule: Decir que + indicative reports what someone says (dice que viene). Decir que + subjunctive tells someone to do something (me dice que venga).
bites.example: Dice que tiene frío y me dice que cierre la ventana.
bites.example_meaning: She says she's cold and tells me to close the window.

bites.title: Ojalá and ¡Que…!
bites.rule: Ojalá always takes the subjunctive. A bare que + subjunctive is a ready-made wish: ¡Que te mejores! ¡Que aproveche! ¡Que tengas suerte! ¡Que lo pases bien!
bites.example: Ojalá tengas suerte en el examen.
bites.example_meaning: I hope you're lucky in the exam.

sorts.title: Infinitive or que + subjunctive?
sorts.why: If one person does both, use the infinitive. If someone else does the second action, use que + subjunctive.

sorts.title: Report or order?

items.text: Mi padre dice que está cansado.
Mi padre me dice que descanse.

sorts.why: Decir que + indicative passes on information; decir que + subjunctive tells someone to do something.

sorts.title: Which wish?

items.text: Your colleagues sit down to lunch.
A friend has a job interview.

sorts.why: ¡Que aproveche! is for meals, ¡Que te mejores! for illness and ¡Que tengas suerte! for a challenge ahead.

spots.sentence: Quiero que vienes a mi casa.
spots.why: Querer que + a different subject takes the subjunctive: vengas.

spots.sentence: Espero que tienes un buen día.
spots.why: Esperar que + a different subject takes the subjunctive: tengas.

spots.sentence: Mi madre quiere que yo estudiar más.
spots.why: After que comes a conjugated verb in the subjunctive, never an infinitive.
Ojalá always takes the subjunctive: haga.

spots.sentence: El médico me recomienda que duermo más.
Ana dice que esté cansada hoy.
spots.why: Ana is reporting how she feels, so decir que takes the indicative: está.

builds.text: Te pido que cierres la puerta.
builds.meaning: I'm asking you to close the door.
I hope you have lots of luck tomorrow.

builds.text: Prefiero cenar en casa esta noche.
builds.meaning: I'd rather have dinner at home tonight.

builds.text: Me dice que la llame luego.
builds.meaning: She tells me to call her later.

realm.content:
## Deseos y peticiones en Eldmark

Quest-givers never say *go*; they say **quiero que vayas a la mazmorra**. When you act yourself, use the infinitive: **quiero ganar el botín**. The paladín **te pide que protejas** Highgate, the maga **te aconseja que no toques** the crystal, and before every raid: **¡Que tengas suerte!**

vocabulary.example: El rey quiere que limpiemos la mazmorra de Deepanvil.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The king wants us to clear the Deepanvil dungeon.

vocabulary.example: La elfa nos pide que la llevemos al Bosque Umbrío.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The elf asks us to take her to the Bosque Umbrío.

vocabulary.example: El enano te aconseja que no entres sin antorcha.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The dwarf advises you not to go in without a torch.

vocabulary.example: El paladín prohíbe que toquemos el cristal.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The paladin forbids us to touch the crystal.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá caiga una espada épica.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Let's hope an epic sword drops.

vocabulary.example: ¿Vas solo a Frostmarch? ¡Que tengas suerte!
vocabulary.example_meaning: You're going to Frostmarch alone? Good luck!

vocabulary.example: El mago quiere que terminemos la misión antes de la noche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage wants us to finish the quest before nightfall.

vocabulary.example: Prefiero que repartamos el botín ahora.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd rather we shared out the loot now.

vocabulary.example: Espero que la mazmorra no esté llena de orcos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the dungeon isn't full of orcs.

bites.title: Quests: que + subjunctive
bites.rule: Someone else must act? que + subjunctive: el rey quiere que vayas. You act yourself? The infinitive: quiero ir.
bites.example: El rey quiere que vayas a Frostmarch.
bites.example_meaning: The king wants you to go to Frostmarch.

listening.text: Quiero que me cures, por favor.
listening.meaning: I want you to heal me, please.

listening.text: Ojalá encontremos la llave de la mazmorra.
listening.meaning: Let's hope we find the dungeon key.

listening.text: La maga nos pide que esperemos aquí.
listening.meaning: The mage asks us to wait here.

listening.text: Te aconsejo que no despiertes al minotauro.
listening.meaning: I advise you not to wake the minotaur.
listening.note: New word: despertar = to wake up.

listening.text: ¡Que tengáis suerte en Highgate!
listening.meaning: Good luck in Highgate, all of you!

builds.text: El paladín quiere que defendamos Highgate.
builds.meaning: The paladin wants us to defend Highgate.

builds.text: Ojalá caiga botín épico esta noche.
builds.meaning: Let's hope epic loot drops tonight.

spots.sentence: El enano quiere que lo ayudamos en la mina.
spots.why: Querer que + a different subject: subjunctive, ayudemos.
Ojalá always takes the subjunctive: encontremos.

sorts.title: Infinitive or que + subjunctive in Eldmark?

items.text: The mage wants us to rest.
I hope to find the loot.
I hope you find the loot.
The dwarf asks us to wait.
We prefer to travel by night.

sorts.why: The same person takes the infinitive; someone else acting takes que + subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: El rey quiere que nosotros ___ la mazmorra.
quiz.explanation: The king wants, we clean: two subjects, so que + subjunctive: limpiemos.
hints: Two different people take the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: El paladín prohíbe que los aprendices ___ (entrar) solos en la mazmorra.
quiz.explanation: Prohibir que + subjunctive. Entro becomes entre, then entren (ellos).
hints: -ar verbs swap to -e; ellos ends in -en.

meadowbrook.content:
## Deseos y peticiones en la granja

In Meadowbrook everyone wants a favour. Rosa **quiere que plantes** fresas, el alcalde **te pide que ayudes** con el festival, and Leo **te aconseja que pesques** por la mañana. Doing it yourself? Use the infinitive: **prefiero cosechar hoy**. And at the tavern, to everyone eating: **¡Que aproveche!**

vocabulary.example: Rosa quiere que plante más fresas esta primavera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa wants me to plant more strawberries this spring.

vocabulary.example: El alcalde nos pide que decoremos la plaza para el festival.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor asks us to decorate the square for the festival.

vocabulary.example: Leo me aconseja que pesque por la mañana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo advises me to fish in the morning.

vocabulary.example: Espero que la vaca dé mucha leche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the cow gives lots of milk.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá crezcan las calabazas antes del otoño.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Let's hope the pumpkins grow before autumn.

vocabulary.example: ¿Ya estáis comiendo la tarta de calabaza? ¡Que aproveche!
vocabulary.example_meaning: Are you already eating the pumpkin pie? Enjoy!

vocabulary.example: Esperamos que la cosecha sea buena este año.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We hope the harvest is good this year.

vocabulary.example: Rosa me recomienda que compre semillas de maíz.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa recommends that I buy corn seeds.

vocabulary.example: El alcalde quiere que todos vengan al festival.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor wants everyone to come to the festival.

bites.title: Favours on the farm
bites.rule: Asking a neighbour to act? pedir / querer / necesitar que + subjunctive. Doing it yourself? Just the infinitive.
bites.example: Necesito que me ayudes con la cosecha.
bites.example_meaning: I need you to help me with the harvest.

listening.text: Rosa quiere que vuelvas mañana a la tienda.
listening.meaning: Rosa wants you to come back to the shop tomorrow.

listening.text: Ojalá pesquemos algo hoy.
listening.meaning: Let's hope we catch something today.
listening.note: Pescar becomes pesquemos, because c becomes qu before e.

listening.text: Te pido que cuides de mis gallinas.
listening.meaning: I'm asking you to look after my hens.
listening.note: New word: cuidar de = to look after.

listening.text: El alcalde prefiere que el festival sea en la playa.
listening.meaning: The mayor prefers the festival to be on the beach.

listening.text: ¡Que lo pases bien en la mina!
listening.meaning: Have a good time in the mine!
listening.note: New word: la mina = the mine.

builds.text: Leo quiere que vayamos al río.
builds.meaning: Leo wants us to go to the river.
I'd rather harvest the corn tomorrow.

spots.sentence: Rosa me pide que planto más fresas.
Ojalá la vaca está mejor mañana.
spots.why: Ojalá always takes the subjunctive: esté.

sorts.title: Report or request on the farm?

items.text: Leo dice que hay peces en el río.
Leo me dice que traiga la caña.
El alcalde dice que el festival es el sábado.
Rosa nos dice que volvamos mañana.
Nora dice que las gallinas están contentas.
Nora me dice que cierre el gallinero.

sorts.why: Decir que + indicative passes on news; decir que + subjunctive asks someone to do something.

quiz.prompt: Leo me aconseja que ___ (pescar) en el río por la mañana.
quiz.explanation: Aconsejar que + subjunctive. Pesco becomes pesque, because c becomes qu to keep the hard sound.
hints: Spelling: c becomes qu before e.

quiz.prompt: Nora: Gracias, pero prefiero ___ las fresas yo sola.
quiz.explanation: Nora prefers and Nora harvests: one person, so the infinitive.

rustwake.content:
## Deseos y peticiones en el páramo

Outside la cúpula everyone asks for something. El capataz Ruiz **quiere que repares** la antena, Marta **te pide que le traigas** agua filtrada, and the radio **dice que hay polvo** (a report: indicative). Going out yourself? **Quiero explorar.** And to every scavenger: **¡Que tengas suerte!**

vocabulary.example: El capataz Ruiz quiere que reparemos la antena hoy.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Foreman Ruiz wants us to repair the antenna today.

vocabulary.example: Marta me pide que le pague con tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta asks me to pay her in nuts.

vocabulary.example: El radiorreloj recomienda que no salgamos con la tormenta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The wrist radio recommends that we don't go out in the storm.

vocabulary.example: La capataza no permite que saquemos agua filtrada de la cúpula.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The forewoman doesn't let us take filtered water out of the Dome.

vocabulary.example: La radio dice que hay polvo en el páramo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The radio says there's dust on the plains.

vocabulary.example: ¿Vas solo al centro comercial en ruinas? ¡Que tengas suerte!
vocabulary.example_meaning: You're going to the ruined shopping centre alone? Good luck!

vocabulary.example: Ojalá no haya una tormenta de ceniza esta noche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Let's hope there's no ash storm tonight.

vocabulary.example: Marta prefiere que le pagues en tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta prefers you to pay her in nuts.

vocabulary.example: Mi radiorreloj me dice que vuelva a la cúpula.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My wrist radio tells me to go back to the Dome.

bites.title: The radio: report or order?
bites.rule: Decir que + indicative reports (la radio dice que hay polvo). Decir que + subjunctive gives an order (Ruiz me dice que vuelva).
bites.example: La radio dice que viene polvo y Ruiz me dice que vuelva.
bites.example_meaning: The radio says dust is coming and Ruiz tells me to come back.

listening.text: Ruiz quiere que vuelvas antes de la noche.
listening.meaning: Ruiz wants you back before nightfall.

listening.text: Ojalá Marta tenga agua filtrada.
listening.meaning: Let's hope Marta has filtered water.
listening.note: New word: el agua filtrada = filtered water.

listening.text: Te pido que no toques ese disco.
listening.meaning: Please don't touch that disc.

listening.text: Necesito que me ayudes a reparar el robot jardinero.
listening.meaning: I need you to help me repair the gardening robot.
listening.note: New word: el robot jardinero = the gardening robot.

listening.text: La radio dice que viene una tormenta.
listening.meaning: The radio says a storm is coming.

builds.text: Marta quiere que le traigas tuercas.
builds.meaning: Marta wants you to bring her nuts.

builds.text: Ruiz me dice que vuelva pronto.
builds.meaning: Ruiz tells me to come back soon.

spots.sentence: El capataz quiere que exploras el páramo.
spots.why: Querer que + a different subject: subjunctive, explores.
Ojalá always takes the subjunctive: haya.

sorts.title: Fact or wish in the wasteland?

items.text: Marta dice que el agua ___ cara. (ser)

sorts.why: Wishes, requests and ojalá take the subjunctive; reporting a fact with decir takes the indicative.

quiz.prompt: El capataz Ruiz me dice que ___ a la cúpula antes de la tormenta. (He tells me to go back.)
quiz.explanation: Decir que as an order takes the subjunctive: vuelva.

quiz.prompt: Marta prefiere que le ___ (pagar, tú) en tuercas.
quiz.explanation: Preferir que + a different subject: subjunctive. Pagar keeps its hard g with gu: pague, pagues.
hints: Spelling: g becomes gu before e.

conversations.title: Before the storm
conversations.scenario: Marta the trader sees Leo the scavenger heading out to the ruined shopping centre.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Leo, ¿vas al centro comercial en ruinas?
lines.meaning: Leo, are you going to the ruined shopping centre?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí. Ruiz quiere que busque piezas para la antena.
lines.meaning: Yes. Ruiz wants me to look for parts for the antenna.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Te pido que me traigas una gaseosa Zafiro.
lines.meaning: Please bring me a Zafiro soda.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Vale, pero quiero que me pagues en tuercas.
lines.meaning: OK, but I want you to pay me in nuts.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Claro. Y te aconsejo que vuelvas antes de la noche.
lines.meaning: Of course. And I'd advise you to come back before nightfall.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Lo sé. El radiorreloj dice que hay polvo.
lines.meaning: I know. The wrist radio says there's dust.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ojalá no te encuentres al escarabajo gigante.
lines.meaning: Let's hope you don't run into the giant beetle.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Yo también lo espero. ¡Que vendas mucho hoy!
lines.meaning: I hope so too. Sell lots today!
